Message body (the text of a message): no fixed format and no version. It is free text that the envelope points to. Result file (where an agent writes its result): the team sets no format. The stage whose brief names the file owns its format, for example the review findings JSON. Built-in or saved pattern record (a team shape) of an unknown version: the run refuses the pattern at start. The refusal names the pattern and the version. No smaller team runs instead.

items.decision: Each inbox (a folder where messages for an agent land) sits in the run directory. The run directory is the git-ignored agent folder, one per feature. The inbox of the contact agent (the agent you talk to) is named by the role name contact, not by session. So a new contact session that takes over the run reads the same inbox. Every other inbox is named by its owner's agent-id. Each message is one envelope file (a small file that says who sent it and where its text is), named by its message id. The team entry script (the one script agents call to start, message and stop agents) writes the file under a temporary name, then renames it. So a wait job (a background process that waits for a file) never sees half a file. After the receiver applies or ignores an envelope, it moves the file to a processed folder beside the inbox. The processed folder is the record of handled messages: a message id already in it is a repeat and changes nothing. The run remembers ids for the whole run. Cleanup deletes the inbox and the processed folder with the run directory. Each inbox stays with its owner by construction, as every run file does: the script builds the path from the run directory and the owner's key.
